about.title: About Fahrenheit to Celsius Converter
about.description: The Fahrenheit to Celsius Converter is a specialized tool for converting temperatures from the Fahrenheit scale to the Celsius scale. This converter is useful for international communication, scientific reference, and everyday temperature understanding. Fahrenheit is primarily used in the United States, while Celsius is the standard in most other countries and scientific applications. Whether you're traveling internationally, following international recipes, or working with scientific data, this tool provides instant Fahrenheit to Celsius conversions using the standard formula.

faq.q: What is the formula for converting Fahrenheit to Celsius?
faq.a: The formula is: °C = (°F - 32) × 5/9. For example, to convert 68°F: (68-32) × 5/9 = 36 × 5/9 = 20°C. Our Fahrenheit to Celsius converter applies this formula automatically for instant results.

faq.q: At what temperature are Fahrenheit and Celsius equal?
faq.a: Fahrenheit and Celsius scales intersect at -40 degrees (-40°F = -40°C). This is the only temperature where both scales show the same numerical value.

faq.q: What are common Fahrenheit to Celsius conversions?
faq.a: Common temperature conversions include: 32°F = 0°C (water freezing), 68°F = 20°C (room temperature), 98.6°F = 37°C (body temperature), 212°F = 100°C (water boiling), and 451°F = 233°C (paper ignition).

faq.q: Why does the United States use Fahrenheit instead of Celsius?
faq.a: The US adopted the Fahrenheit scale before the metric system became internationally standardized. Fahrenheit provides more granular whole numbers for everyday weather temperatures, with 0-100°F covering most climate conditions.

faq.q: How accurate is this Fahrenheit to Celsius converter?
faq.a: Our converter uses the exact mathematical formula with decimal precision, making it suitable for scientific reference, cooking, and weather analysis.

faq.q: How do I convert 100 degrees Fahrenheit to Celsius?
faq.a: 100°F converts to 37.78°C using the formula: (100-32) × 5/9 = 68 × 5/9 = 37.78°C. This temperature is close to normal human body temperature.
